extracted.intended_audience: academics, policy makers, and the general public interested in open access to research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative criteria arguing that publicly funded academic research should be made openly accessible and communicated in more public-facing, less paywalled ways. Focus is on publication venue choice, transparency, and public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access for publicly funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic research is publicly funded -- why isn't it publicly available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes fund academic research at public universities, so the results should be accessible to the public rather than locked behind paywalls; the page frames public availability as an expectation tied to public funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish in more accessible media
rubrics_metrics.description: Academics should publish in more accessible media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to choose publication venues or formats that are accessible to non-specialists and the general public instead of relying solely on expensive, for-profit journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an open-access relationship between public and scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for a new, open-access relationship between the public and scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes reciprocal, transparent interactions where research is shared openly with the public, facilitating understanding and potential participation rather than keeping scholarship isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paywalls and bureaucratic barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of research happening behind paywalls and bureaucracy, wouldn't it be better if it was unfolding right in front of us?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies paywalls and institutional bureaucracy as anti-patterns that obstruct public access; recommends reducing these barriers so research can be experienced and scrutinized publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize public education and democratic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: "A functioning democracy requires that the public be well-educated and well-informed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions access to research as a democratic imperative: researchers and publishers should consider the societal role of research dissemination in supporting an informed citizenry.
